subject: Offer calibration: compensation taxonomy and localized uplift checklist
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Emma Ramos <emma@acmebio.com>

Subject: Offer calibration: compensation taxonomy and localized uplift checklist

Team —

As we ramp hiring for Platform (SRE + Serving Runtime) in Q2, I want to lock down the compensation taxonomy we’ll use for outbound offers into regional markets. This thread will be the source of truth for a couple of quick decisions the recruiting and finance teams need by next Friday.

Goal: finalize a compact checklist that ties level -> band -> local uplift rules so recruiters can calculate OTE and target base with minimal back-and-forth. High level constraints below:

- Keep base tiers consistent across US core markets with a multiplier for high-cost metros.
- Use benchmarked midpoints based on recent comps (attached geo-benchmarks-Q1-2027.pdf).
- Preserve total offer band width for senior ICs to allow negotiation room (+5%/-5% guardrails).
- Any role-specific premium (hard-to-find skills) should be expressed as an explicit uplift from the band midpoint and approved by hiring manager + finance.

Open decisions I need input on:
1) Do we keep the current band names (L3-L6) or move to a numeric anchor (e.g., IC3 -> Band 3) for clarity in offer letters?
2) For CA metros (SF/LA), do we hard-cap base uplift at +18% vs national midpoint, or do we allow up to +22% for VP-level hires?
3) Should we require a one-page justification doc (template attached: localization-checklist.docx) for any uplift >12%?

Action items:
- Laura: please review the attached comp_grid_v2.xlsx and confirm midpoints/50th percentiles.
- Marissa: flag any roles where we should add a skill premium (e.g., custom CUDA + 8-bit quantization).
- Vivek: do we need an exception path for strategic hires that bypasses the standard cap?

Emma — I included you so Acme Bio can confirm your target bands for the open Staff ML Eng role (we discussed a 30–34k delta from national midpoint). If you prefer, we can run a quick phone calibration.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Talent Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Offer calibration: compensation taxonomy and localized uplift checklist

Irene — thanks for the clear brief. I reviewed comp_grid_v2.xlsx and the geo benchmarks. Summary comments below; I left inline notes in the sheet.

Quick summary:
- Band naming: recommend we keep L-prefixed titles (L3-L6) in internal systems but translate to Band numbers in offer templates. That keeps org chart clarity and simplifies external comms.
- CA metro uplift: agree with a standard +18% cap for individual contributor levels; allow an exception path up to +22% for Director+ (requires VP sign-off and note to compensation committee).
- Justification doc: enforce for uplift >10% (not 12%). The smaller threshold reduces ad-hoc exceptions and forces hiring managers to justify where market data is weak.
- Skill premiums: suggested fixed skill premium buckets (e.g., CUDA/LLM infra +8%, Quantization specialist +6%) as standalone line items in offer calculations.

I attached a cleaned version of the comp grid with midpoints adjusted using our trailing 6-month offer data and Marketbench Q1. See tab 'proposed_midpoints'.

Open questions for finance ops: what friction does a 10% justification threshold create? If acceptable, I’ll update the offer templates and recruiter SOPs.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Total Rewards | Redwood Inference

- Serving Runtime Eng (IC5): market demand for low-latency architect / CUDA experience is strong; I recommend a 10% skill premium baseline for interviews moving to offers.
- SRE (IC4): markets around NYC and SF show a 7–9% uplift vs national midpoint; recommend we allow up to +12% without justification because retention risk is high for this cohort.
- Candidate example (Acme Bio): Emma shared expectations — they’re expecting a +14% uplift on national midpoint for a Staff ML Eng. We should either match or present stronger non-cash comp (signing +RSU).

I attached one redline in the comp grid for the Serving Runtime roles.

Irene/Laura/Marissa —
Short: yes, we need an exception path for strategic hires. Proposal: exceptions evaluated by a 3-person panel (Mgr+VP+Comp). Panel approves increase above cap up to 25% from national midpoint; anything >25% requires executive committee sign-off. Decision should be logged to HRREQ record (I’ll work with ops to add a quick approval form).

Also — finance flagged that allowing a no-justification window up to 12% for SRE across SF/NYC could materially increase spend. Suggest we treat those as higher probability and budget headroom accordingly rather than breaking the cap. We can run a quick headcount impact model if recruiting sends anticipated offers by role/market.

Quick update and next steps —

Thanks all for the input. Decisions captured below (and I updated the comp_grid_v2.xlsx in Drive — see link).

Decisions (final):
- Keep internal L-nomenclature; translate to Band N in offers.
- CA metros: standard cap +18% for ICs; Director+ exception up to +22% via VP sign-off.
- Justification doc required for uplift >10% (Mar 22 proposal adopted).
- Skill premiums: implement fixed buckets (CUDA +8%, Quant +6%, Sparse/KV-cache infra +5%).
- Exceptions: 3-person panel (Hiring Manager + VP + Comp) can approve up to 25%; >25% needs exec committee and must be logged in HRREQ-1247.
- SRE baseline uplift: allow up to +12% in SF/NYC without justification but tag forecasted spend; finance will model impact next week.

Action items:
- Laura: please push the updated offer templates to the templates repo and publish the recruiter SOP by EOD Mon 4/4.
- Marissa: draft the fast-edits playbook for recruiters and link to the checklist.
- Vivek: create the panel approval form in HRREQ and add the logging field.
- Emma: we’ll route a formal offer to Acme candidate within the 48-hour window upon template update.

If there are concerns with any final decision, reply-all within 48 hours; otherwise I’ll close the thread and we’ll move to operationalization.

Thanks —
Irene
Head of Talent Operations | Redwood Inference
